clue.text: Take MI5 literally at first, which is wrong

indicators.note: says the MI5 piece comes at the front, before the other word

parts.note: the figure 5 read as the letter it looks like, S, turning MI5 into these letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that reading the name of Britain's security service too literally leads you astray.
explanation.walkthrough: MI5 is Britain's domestic security service; 'literally' asks you to read its 5 as the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, used as a noun, is an error or blunder, which is what a slip of judgement amounts to.

clue.text: Softy types in shaggy hair

indicators.note: the types word is placed inside the hair word

parts.note: an unruly mass of hair is called a mop
ilks are kinds or types

explanation.surface: Gentle sorts sporting unkempt hairstyles.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, weak, feeble person is a softy, the old word for one lacking spirit.

clue.text: Cartesian settlement of religious differences

indicators.note: settling the letters means rearranging them into a resolved new order

explanation.surface: Descartes's philosophy is offered as a resolution of religious quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes conflict or division between religious groups or sects.

clue.text: Bitter maple, a little bit

parts.note: Acer is the botanical name for the maple genus

indicators.note: only the first letter of bit is taken

explanation.surface: A maple tree's sap described as slightly sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for sour or harsh-tasting, a synonym for bitter.

clue.text: 24, taking belt, troubled old king

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, a word for anaesthetic or the upper air

explanation.surface: Someone taking a belt to an ancient monarch who was having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' signals rearranging ETHER (from 24) together with BELT.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventh-century king of Kent, the first English king converted to Christianity, bore this name.

clue.text: Academic department is defective without starting course

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the faulty word wraps round the letter

parts.note: defective means faulty

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word course is the one taken

explanation.surface: A university department is complained of as useless for lacking an introductory course.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's faculty is one of its main academic divisions, such as the faculty of law.

clue.text: Currency no longer has honest sound

indicators.note: the word sound tells us the entry only sounds like the word for honest

parts.note: frank means honest and outspoken

explanation.surface: An old coinage is said to have an honest ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French franc was replaced by the euro in 2002, so it is a currency no longer used.

clue.text: What Equity achieves stops future generations

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' union, which deals with casting pay, so it sets cast rates
Equity is the British actors' union, which deals with casting pay, so it sets cast rates

explanation.surface: The actors' union is accused of preventing future generations being born.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' trade union; read it as fixing CAST RATES, the pay for a cast.
explanation.definitionFit: To neuter a male animal by removing the testicles prevents it from fathering offspring.

clue.text: Plunders a little treasure in battle

indicators.note: the small piece goes inside the battle name

parts.note: Loos was a First World War battle in France

indicators.note: just the first letter of treasure is used

explanation.surface: Raiders carry off a small amount of valuables during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Loos (1915) was a major British offensive in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot is to plunder or pillage, so the plural verb matches 'Plunders'.

clue.text: His delivery may be 5 short

annotationWithheld.why: His delivery may be 5 short (7): YIELDER; a cryptic definition whose reference '5 short' cannot be explained from 5-across or 5-down, and no source gives the parse

clue.text: Cash, whereof a little is needed in inducement

definitions.text: Cash, whereof a little is needed in inducement

indicators.note: the small piece must be placed inside the inducement word

parts.note: an inducement is a lure, a bait to tempt someone

indicators.note: only a scrap of the word Cash is used, its first letter

explanation.surface: A remark that money plays a part in any bribe or temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: filthy money is exactly what gets put inside a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a slightly scornful term for money, especially money gained dishonourably, as with a bribe.

clue.text: Jagger's monument?

parts.note: Mick Jagger fronts the Rolling Stones, so he is the leading member of that band; read as a grave marker, the phrase is a pun

explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker is a slab set at the top end of a burial plot, a memorial to the dead.

clue.text: Rough description of government claim? Bosh!

indicators.note: rough handling knocks these letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a government's boast, waved away with an exclamation of contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is the signal: the letters of CLAIM and BOSH rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaotic, disorganised administration is often called by this informal adjective meaning messily mismanaged.

clue.text: Built up, they say, but actually the reverse

indicators.note: signals that the word for built up is only heard, the entered word sounding like it

parts.note: built up means raised

explanation.surface: A building said to have gone up has in truth come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry sounds like the word for built up but means the opposite: flattened, demolished.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of building something up is knocking it flat, and this spelling means demolished.

clue.text: An old soldier abroad is in the hunt for spoil, unless restrained

indicators.note: the letters are held captive within the words spoil, unless

explanation.surface: A veteran overseas joins the search for plunder, provided he is held in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained' says the letters are held inside SPOIL, UNLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A French infantryman of the First World War was nicknamed this, a soldier from abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Other clue than I set is not cricket

indicators.note: the letters are set out again, arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A compiler complains that a rival's clue is unsporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' signals rearranging CLUE and THAN I; 'not cricket' is the British idiom for unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair or dishonourable behaviour, that is, morally wrong.

clue.text: One able to stretch tales more wildly …

indicators.note: letters thrown around wildly fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who exaggerates more extravagantly than others spins taller stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' says the letters of TALES and MORE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastic polymer such as rubber is a substance that stretches and springs back.

clue.text: Leo's friend also has about 100 parts

parts.note: and means also

indicators.note: the parts word goes about, round, the hundred

parts.note: roles are acting parts
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: Someone's companion also has around a hundred roles to play.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable, the slave pulled a thorn from a lion's paw, and the lion later spared him; Leo means lion.
explanation.definitionFit: The slave of legend who befriended a lion is the lion's friend, Leo being Latin for lion.

clue.text: Prophet taking note of mineral

parts.note: Malachi is the last of the Old Testament prophets
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A prophet takes note of a green stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A green copper carbonate used in ornaments is a mineral of this name.

clue.text: … once named over being too cocky …

indicators.note: the naming word is draped over, covering, the other word, so it wraps round it

parts.note: to be named in a report is to be cited
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone singled out in the past for being overconfident.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'over' cannot mean above; here it means covering, so the naming word wraps round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vain and excessively self-satisfied is too cocky, full of themselves.

clue.text: Soccer team from Cinque Port lacking victory

indicators.note: the victory word is missing from the port's name

parts.note: Winchelsea is an ancient town in the Cinque Ports, a group of English Channel ports
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A football club from an old Channel port that has failed to win.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are historic towns on England's south-east coast; dropping WIN from WINCHELSEA leaves the London club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Premier League club from west London is a soccer team of this name.

clue.text: … as Yugoslavia did in Croatia?

definitions.meaning: Yugoslavia broke apart into separate states in the 1990s
a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia goes by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Yugoslavia broke up into separate countries, and a Croatian Adriatic port has the same name.

clue.text: Writer of trifle containing lost letters

indicators.note: the trifle word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value

indicators.note: the letters of lost are taken loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor author's work has letters that went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is an unusual anagram signal: read 'lost letters' as the letters of lost, freed to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian author of War and Peace is a famous writer.

clue.text: Biblical character, one rejected by church

indicators.note: a word thrown back is turned round, so the letters of one run backwards

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture who was turned away by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genesis patriarch, father of Methuselah, said to have walked with God, bears this name.

clue.text: Do overtime at the pictures

indicators.note: turned over, the little word is read backwards

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Working extra hours at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A British cinema chain whose name came to mean any cinema, that is, the pictures.

clue.text: Established state belonging to France

parts.note: something established beyond doubt is proven
Cal is a short form of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A settled nation said to be French property.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes Provence, a region of southern France, so it belongs to France.

clue.text: Wine brought round in a large measure

indicators.note: the round letter is placed in the measure

parts.note: a pint is a generous measure of drink
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Wine served by the pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot, as in Pinot Noir or Pinot Grigio, is a grape and the wine made from it.

clue.text: One missing from a choice of two can put you out

indicators.note: the one is absent from the choice word

parts.note: either introduces a choice between two
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dropping an option from two choices could knock you unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: An early anaesthetic, inhaled to make patients unconscious, so it can put you out.

clue.text: Gore with god's backing is able to find a way in the Middle East

indicators.note: the god's name goes into reverse, read backwards

parts.note: Zeus is the chief Greek god
is able means can
Al Gore, the former US vice-president, supplies his first name

explanation.surface: A politician, with divine support, manages to find a route through the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gore' looks like stabbing, but it is Al Gore, giving AL; 'backing' reverses ZEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterway through Egypt linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea is a shipping route in the Middle East.

clue.text: Man's given time for robbery

parts.note: read as man is, a male pronoun plus is gives these letters

explanation.surface: A man is sentenced to time in jail for a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' is a contraction of man is, so HE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring robbery, especially of a bank or jeweller, is called by this informal word.

clue.text: Ring from alien after yearly article is dropped

indicators.note: the alien comes after the shortened word
the article is taken out of the yearly word

parts.note: yearly means annual
A is the indefinite article
ET, the film's extraterrestrial, is the standard crossword alien

explanation.surface: A ring obtained from an extraterrestrial once an annual item is discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dropped' removes A from ANNUAL, leaving ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture and heraldry a small ring or ring-shaped band goes by this name.

clue.text: Church regretful about witchcraft

indicators.note: the regretful word goes round the church letters

parts.note: regretful means sorry
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church expresses remorse over a past of persecuting witches.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic using supernatural powers, especially evil ones, is a synonym for witchcraft.
